species.name: Leatherjack

dex.text: A tough little grub that chews the lawn from underneath and is surprisingly well liked by rooks. It has no legs and no complaints.
dex.fact: A leatherjacket is the larva of a crane fly, and it lives in the soil eating grass roots, often for most of a year.

species.real: Starlings, rooks and gulls probe lawns and fields for leatherjackets, and a large flock can clear a lot of them.

species.name: Husk

dex.text: A tarry case with two horns and a slit. Something is in there thinking about it, and its eyes glow if you look in.
dex.fact: A crane fly spends the winter as a larva or pupa in the soil, then the adult crawls out of the pupal case to emerge in late summer.

species.real: The pupal case of a crane fly has two small horns at its head end, which it uses to push its way up through the soil.

species.name: Longlegs

dex.text: All legs and apology, bumping into the lampshade at night. It cannot bite or sting, and is quite put out when people think it can.
dex.fact: Adult crane flies are harmless; they do not bite or sting, and many live for only a few days, just long enough to find a mate.

species.real: A crane fly can shed a leg to escape a predator, which is why so many daddy-long-legs are found missing one.
